hypothesis: The neuron responds strongly to discrete, high-contrast dark features—typically black, dark brown, or navy blue—set against a lighter, often neutral background such as white, beige, silver, or light natural tones. The activating visual elements are varied but consistently involve bold, defined shapes, including geometric patterns (dots, circular spots, stripes), alphanumeric characters, or specific anatomical regions (animal facial masks, noses, eyes, wing tips, and spines). The neuron remains invariant to object identity (activating for insects, mammals, ceramics, and cardboard text alike), surface texture, and scene context, as long as the sharp dark-on-light luminance contrast is preserved. The activating feature typically occupies 10–40% of the image area and is predominantly positioned in the center or upper-middle portion of the frame.
